item.title: Araghchi slams western media’s ‘Iraq War-style’ disinformation

item.title: Iran FM Araghchi receives Qatari delegation in Muscat
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who is visiting Muscat for an official visit to Oman, received a Qatari delegation on Tuesday afternoon. The Qatari delegation, headed by an adviser to Qatar’s prime minister, traveled to Oman and held talks with Iran’s foreign minister on the latest regional developments. Referring to Qatar’s continued role in efforts to ease tensions in the region, Araghchi stressed the importance of continued consultations among regional countries to counter the destabilizing and insecurity-inducing activities of actors from outside the region

item.title: : Iran Oman and Uzbekistan hold trilateral foreign ministers’ meeting in Muscat
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who is visiting Muscat for an official visit to Oman and consultations with senior Omani officials on bilateral relations and regional developments, attended a trilateral meeting of the foreign ministers of Iran, Oman and Uzbekistan to discuss the potential of the North-South Corridor. The meeting, hosted by Sayyid Badr Al-Busaidi, Foreign Minister of the Sultanate of Oman, was attended by Bakhtiyor Saidov, Foreign Minister of the Republic of Uzbekistan, and Araghchi. The three sides discussed ways to expand interregional cooperation in various economic, trade, transportation and transit sectors. Highlighting the considerable potential of the three countries to expand economic ties, particularly through strengthening trade exchanges along the Central Asia–Persian Gulf/Gulf of Oman route (the North-South Corridor), the foreign ministers of Iran, Uzbekistan and Oman emphasized the importance of planning to expand regional transportation networks and complete and upgrade the relevant infrastructure

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran considers the issuance of unjust sentences against a group of Bahraini clerics and citizens on spurious pretexts to be a systematic and widespread violation of human rights and strongly condemns it. The imposition of unjust life and lengthy prison sentences and the confiscation of religious scholars’ property, shortly after the disgraceful remarks made by the US Secretary of State against clerics and prominent figures of the Shia world, demonstrate the Bahraini rulers’ alignment with the US establishment’s efforts to foment religious discord. Undoubtedly, holding show trials and using the judicial system as a cover for the collective punishment and harassment of clerics and ordinary Bahraini citizens can in no way conceal the inhumane nature of this action or its incompatibility with the fundamental principles and norms of human rights. The leveling of entirely baseless and unfounded accusations, including alleged links with Iran, as grounds for the criminal prosecution of Bahraini citizens and their collective sentencing to lengthy prison terms, is a clear indication of the Bahraini rulers’ abuse of the judiciary to suppress any rights advocacy. This, in turn, will undermine the credibility of Bahrain’s judicial system, render the issued verdicts null and void, and further erode the legitimacy and public acceptance of the ruling class in the country. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, while firmly rejecting the baseless allegations leveled against Iran, calls on the Bahraini rulers to end their repression of the people and religious scholars and to respect their human and civil rights in accordance with human rights standards and Islamic teachings. It also emphasizes that a policy of repression and intimidation can in no way prevent the people of Bahrain from pursuing their legitimate and rightful demands.

item.title: Iranian Pakistani Foreign Ministers hold talks in Islamabad
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi, who is in Islamabad to attend the meeting of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO), met with Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar on Monday afternoon. Araghchi thanked Pakistan for its warm hospitality and the successful organization of the 30th meeting of the ECO Council of Foreign Ministers, emphasizing the need to strengthen multilateral cooperation, enhance economic and trade interactions, and expand coordination among member states. The two foreign ministers exchanged views on developing and expanding bilateral relations in areas of mutual interest. Araghchi and Ishaq Dar also reviewed regional and international developments and discussed the latest diplomatic efforts aimed at safeguarding regional stability and security.

Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi met with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad on Monday afternoon, along with other foreign ministers and senior officials attending the 30th Meeting of the ECO Council of Foreign Ministers. Sharif welcomed the foreign ministers of ECO member states, stressing the importance of strengthening regional cooperation and utilizing the member countries' extensive capacities to expand economic, trade and transit ties among neighboring and regional countries. The foreign ministers thanked Pakistan for hosting the summit and successfully organizing its 30th session, emphasizing the need to strengthen multilateral cooperation, expand economic and trade relations, and promote greater convergence among member states. Araghchi, referring to the productive discussions at the summit, particularly on Palestine and the strong condemnation of the genocide in the occupied Palestinian territories, stressed the urgent need for the international community and Islamic countries to address the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and the West Bank. Referring to a clause in the summit's final statement supporting Iran's proposed initiative to end the imposed war, Araghchi also praised Pakistan's efforts as a mediator in Iran-US negotiations. Sharif, in turn, underscored Pakistan's and the Muslim world's commitment to the Palestinian cause, describing the crimes committed against the Palestinian people in Gaza and the West Bank as a catastrophe for humanity and emphasizing everyone's moral and humanitarian responsibility to confront the continuation of these crimes.

item.title: Iranian Russian FMs discuss diplomatic efforts to preserve regional global peace
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi held a phone conversation with his Russian counterpart, Sergey Lavrov, at noon on Monday to discuss the latest political and diplomatic efforts and initiatives aimed at preserving regional and global peace and security. Araghchi, who is in Islamabad to attend the 30th Meeting of the ECO Council of Ministers of Foreign Affairs, held the telephone conversation with Lavrov during his visit.
